Source: http://www.canoe.ca/CalgarySun

Posted August 7, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: Canadian papers are generally much better in their coverage of the marijuana issues than those in DEAland.

However, when the papers owned by the Canoe partnership address the subject, they confuse snideness with intelligence. They take a tone of intellectual and moral superiority, and then proceed to make complete fools of themselves.

The first item below is an Op-ed that seems to be based on the pathetic London (Ontario) Free Press – another Canoe paper-- editorial, that I posted last week.

See
We Have Reefer Madness Award Winner! Absurdity and Incoherence in Ontario.

Like the second item, a letter to the editors of two more Canoe papers, the Ottawa Sun and Calgary Sun, the Op-ed below is in response to the Ontario Appeal Court ruling.
See

Canadian Court Says Lack of Provision for Medical Marijuana Violates Fundamental Rights; Gives Parliament 12 Months to Fix Marijuana Prohibition -- Or There Will Be No Marijuana Laws in Canada.

And the author seems not to have read the decision.

In fairness to all concerned, the columnist and even most of the Canoe papers, other than the ridiculous London Free Press, seem to have resigned themselves to the reality of medical marijuana, but just barely.

Ultimately, the marijuana reform movement in Canada may also have the effect of reforming these dregs of Canadian journalism. Marijuana is very much on the public agenda in Canada and the Canadian people deserve much better from these papers.

Journalism at this level may be unavoidable in DEAland, but it is grotesquely incongruous in a country where people are genuinely trying to deal with the issues.)



August 5, 2000
From The Calgary Sun
callet@sunpub.com
http://www.canoe.ca/CalgarySun/
http://www.canoe.ca/Chat/home.html
By Linda Williamson

WHY I'M NOT HIGH ON LEGALIZING POT

Toronto - For a group of people who claim to be mellow, live-and-let types, marijuana activists can get pretty worked up.

A supposedly landmark decision by the Ontario Court of Appeal, which technically struck down the ban on pot possession, has set them off from coast to coast, declaring the day for decriminalization was high - er, nigh.

You'd have thought the judges had made the stuff legal. But the truth is, they were only trying to make life easier for folks who need marijuana for medical reasons. The reason they suspended the law for 12 months was basically to light a fire under the feds - fix the law or all of Ontario will be up in smoke (or rather, smoking up) come next August.

In fact, the court specifically noted that this was a case where simply striking down the law " poses a danger to the public. " Exactly.
(MarijuanaNews note: Not exactly. What the judge actually said was, " I also agree with the Crown that the declaration of invalidity should be suspended to provide Parliament with the opportunity to fill the void. Such a declaration is required where striking down a provision " poses a potential [Emphasis added] danger to the public " : Schachter at p. 715. I would suspend the declaration of invalidity for 12 months. "

In other words, what they said was having no marijuana laws " poses a potential [Emphasis added] danger to the public " – and certainly the Crown would have sought just such a delay if the Judges had not granted one. Inasmuch as there would be no laws restricting use even by children, and these judges definitely were not into reefer madness, then all that one might say is that having no laws " poses a potential danger to the public. " )

Medical use is one thing, but Canada is far from ready for legalization of pot, or even decriminalization.
(MarijuanaNews note: Excuse me, but surveys consistently show that two thirds of Canadians favor decrim.)

Yes, I'm well aware - thanks in part to all those activists who are avid writers of letters to the editor - of the case for decriminalization, which is backed by the Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police. Let's face it, cops already turn a blind eye to a lot of pot use - as you can see at any rock concert.
See
Favorable Reaction By Prohibitionist Canadian Press and Police To Chiefs’ Recommendation To " Decriminalize " Marijuana Bodes Well
– Cover For The Politicians – 2 Articles

And I would agree it's time for a full, open discussion about our marijuana laws. But first the activists are going to have to admit a few things about their miracle weed.
(MarijuanaNews note: If we are going to have such a discussion, and the Canadian people will have it, then the least that " journalists " can do is not lie to their readers.

And might it be too much for prohibitionists too admit a few things about marijuana prohibition?

After all, the choice is not whether there is going to be marijuana -- even this writer acknowledges that -- but whether people are going to be arrested for using, growing it, selling it. It will also be about the problems created by contraband markets.)



For one thing, it will have to be regulated. Yes, it's " natural ", but we're talking about a mind-altering substance. Today's pot is up to 2,500 times more potent than the stuff aging boomers might have experimented with in college.
(MarijuanaNews note: When I saw this absurd number in the London Free Press editorial I just assumed that they were careless and had meant to write " percent " -- instead of " times. " That would still be wrong, but at least it would be close to the party line.

However, Ms Williamson seems to have swallowed this nonsense whole. The average potency of Canadian marijuana is around six percent, according to the RCMP.)

See
RCMP Annual Report On the " Drug Situation in Canada " Contradicts Staples Of the Prohibitionist Party Line. Exclusive To MarijuanaNews.

This stuff can have you practically hallucinating after a couple of tokes. So don't try to tell me it doesn't impair people's faculties and that users don't endanger anyone.
(MarijuanaNews note: Bluntly, this is a violation of the 9th Commandment. This is false evidence given for the purpose of encouraging the arrest of millions of Canadians. No one is " practically hallucinating after a couple of tokes " of any marijuana. Ms Williamson may have hallucinated that sentence.)
See
Marijuana Prohibition, Media Criticism, Copyrights and the 8th and 9th Commandments.
Pot devotees, of course, will swear to you they actually drive, etc. better when they're stoned - even as they're bursting out laughing at the joke someone told 10 minutes ago.

One study in 1994 found 276 drivers killed in accidents had used pot.
(MarijuanaNews note: Again, this is from the London Free Press. That is an utterly meaningless statement. Never mind that the tests do not show that they were actually stoned at the time of the accident. It should be obvious to anyone capable of rational thought that there is difference between correlation and causation. There are millions of marijuana smokers, so if none of them were ever in accidents, we should make marijuana use mandatory. However, I favor that drastic measure only for certain editorialists.)
See
Canadian Study Confirms That Marijuana Impairs Driving Far Less Than Alcohol

We still know very little about the effects of this drug. You can't tell how strong it is and it's difficult to control how much you're ingesting.
(MarijuanaNews note: The first half of that sentence is blaming marijuana for a consequence of marijuana prohibition. Contraband markets generally do not have standards.

The second point is simply untrue. One of the great advantages of smoking is that it allows the user to control the dosage. For example, when a drug is taken orally, a drink or a pill, the absorption of the drug is influenced by many factors, including whether the person has eaten recently, the health of their digestive system, etc. Moreover, a person will not know for some time, perhaps an hour or more, whether the dose has been adequate, or excessive.

The onset of effects of smoking are known in minutes. That is the great advantage to smoking as a means of administration. This is as true of recreational use as medical.)

See
Why would anyone want to smoke a medicine? Isn't smoking per se bad for you?

There's no breathalyzer-type test of impairment, and we don't really know if it's addictive, or how long-term use affects the body.
(MarijuanaNews note: From the statements of fact in the Clay case
http://www.ontariocourts.on.ca/decisions/2000/july/clay.htm
 " 5. Cannabis is not an addictive substance. "
There were similar findings of fact in the recent BC court case.)
See
British Columbia Court Rules Two to One That Marijuana Possession Laws Must Be
Decided By Parliament. Dissent Makes Hearing By Supreme Court Likely. Facts Make
Marijuana Prohibition Look Bad, Again.
and
Is marijuana addictive?

A few activists admit these risks, though of course they blame the law.
(MarijuanaNews note: And just how many anti-prohibitionists’ work has she studied so that she knows what " a few " say.)

 " The black market prevents you from having any quality control, " says David Malmo-Levine, who's fighting his B.C. possession conviction up to the Supreme Court.

At least he conceded, in an interview with the Winnipeg Sun, that smoking pot can be harmful. This would seem evident to any non-smoker (of tobacco, I mean - now that stuff should be illegal) - all that inhaling can't be good for the lungs.

Malmo-Levine advocates " harm reduction " methods, including using a water bong and taking vitamin C. Also, know what strain you're smoking. (How? Where's the label?)

" Smoke organic, high-potency marijuana during high-pleasure, low-stress activities and you will do no harm to yourself or anybody else, " he advises. Great. But what about those who don't follow those mellow guidelines?

There's also the matter of organized crime which controls the drug trade. You think that's going to go away with a court ruling?
(MarijuanaNews note: Where is the organized crime in the legal drug businesses?)

Obviously, I'm not what you'd call a pot person. Legal or not, it wouldn't affect my life much since I've never been a big fan of the culture - I don't particularly like the passing-the-joint thing, the loss of control, the stupid stoner stare, and I hate any kind of smoke.

Yes, alcohol can be evil, but it's more pleasant to imbibe, easier to pace oneself and and generally makes for more convivial conversation.
See
Canada's Crime Rate Dropped In 1999 For 8th Consecutive Year Without Creating A Police State. But Marijuana Arrests Continue to Climb. Alcohol Related Violence Soars in UK. Lessons for Everyone.

Once some of the basic questions about health risks are answers, I wouldn't object to more accessible , carefully controlled and labelled marijuana, perhaps sold in liquor stores (as cigarettes should be.)

After all. with an estimated 2.5 million users, it's pretty prevalent anyway. As one pot paraphernalia retailer said: " Sales are booming now. If it becomes legal, it's not like you will see a massive increase in consumption. "

But let's not kid ourselves. As Malmo-Levine says, " Just because it's fun doesn't mean it's not medicine. "

Indeed. And medicine can de dangerous.
(MarijuanaNews note: So can bad journalism.)

Copyright: 2000 The Calgary Sun

August 5, 2000
From The Calgary Sun and Ottawa Sun
editor@sunpub.com
http://www.canoe.ca/OttawaSun/
http://www.canoe.ca/CalgarySun/home.html
callet@sunpub.com
(MarijuanaNews note: The Canoe papers have the custom of appending comments at the end of letters to the editor. They are usually rather snide when the letter writer is anti-prohibitionist. In this case, the writer plays to their prejudices so they made this one the " Letter of the Day " in both the Calgary and Ottawa papers, and they were too, too, too kind.

The letter writer obviously has not read the opinion, but the editors seem not to have read it either.)



Regarding legalizing marijuana for the sick. What I can't understand is why these people who so desperately need cannabis for medical reasons not use the THC pill?

It delivers all the active ingredient of marijuana without the toxic side effect of smoking. I've read that the cost for the pill is approximately $1 US.
(MarijuanaNews note: The 25mg pill sells for around C$3, but is much more expensive in DEAland.)

The drug is called dronabinol (tradename Marinol) and is manufactured in the U.S.A. by Unimed Pharmaceuticals of Buffalo Grove, Ill. (In Canada, Sanofi-Synthelabo Canada) It is approved in Canada for weight loss associated with wasting syndrome.
(MarijuanaNews note: From the opinion, which is online at
http://www.ontariocourts.on.ca/decisions/2000/july/parker.htm
" Marinol is also essentially useless for acute situations. Smoked marihuana, on the other hand, can be used by persons who feel nausea coming over them, because it delivers the THC quickly and more effectively than Marinol. Marihuana gives acute relief of nausea and vomiting… Finally, Marinol, since it only contains THC, is of no use to individuals, particularly epileptic patients, who benefit from CBD… "

" [57] The trial judge found that smoking marihuana is more efficient and at least five times faster in delivering THC and CBD to the blood stream than oral medication and, for people like Parker, more effective. " )

Have those " legalize marijuana " activists who care so much about the sick offered this pill?

It is a lot less risky for the sick to take, not having any of the side effects of smoking.
See
Counterblaste to DEA: Fallacious Pharmacology.
" The contention that smoking cannot possibly be an acceptable route for the administration
of a therapeutic substance is morality dressed up as science. " by Peter Webster

My guess is these activists haven't offered it to the sick and not because they haven't heard it, but that its convenient for them not to speak about it. But unfortunately not so convenient for the sick.
(MarijuanaNews note: First, of course, it is not the place of medical marijuana " activists " to " offer " Marinol or anything else. What we are arguing is that the sick and dying should not be arrested for using medical marijuana.

Second, there are numerous stories about Marinol on this site and most other anti-prohibitionist sites, but one would have to read something to know this.)
See
Marinol Was The First Schedule 2 Drug To Be " Down-Scheduled, "
Boasts Roxanne On Its New Marinol.com Web Site.
Doesn’t That Mean That It Should Never Have Been Schedule 2 Anyway?

So the real agenda is exposed, that is they're not interested in the welfare of the sick, but more interested in getting high.
See
Is medical marijuana just the opening wedge to legalize marijuana generally?

It all comes off to me as if those who want to legalize marijuana to intoxicate themselves want to use our sympathy for the sick as a shield.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is terribly insulting to patients like Terry Parker and Jim Wakeford and many others who have had to fight for their rights. Then along comes this ignoramus who hasn't even read the opinion but claims that the patients are just pawns of the evil " legalize marijuana " activists. As a reward, the editors say that this is the " letter of the day. "

They owe an apology to the brave medical marijuana patients who have fought their governments to get recognition of their most basic rights.)

As if we need more intoxicated people on our planet, in our homes and on our roads.

Robert Mollot, Ottawa

Ottawa Sun: (You make a good point, but we understand there's more to marijuana than just THC)
(MarijuanaNews note: If they " understand there's more to marijuana than just THC " – which is covered in the opinion at great length, then they should understand that the entire premise of the letter is false. So what " good point " did he make?)

Calgary Sun: (Some chronically ill might benefit, but the motives of many others are highly suspicious.)

(MarijuanaNews note: If " some chronically ill might benefit, " then the advocates of medical marijuana are right, whatever their motives.

What then are the motives of those who oppose something that would help " some chronically " ill people? Or are only the motives of anti-prohibitionists subject to question?)
